name: Casco Historico (Old Town)
tagline: The pink-red heart within the walls
description: The walled historic core, stacked earthen houses in that famous rust-pink hue along steep, hanging lanes up to the cathedral and castle ruins. This is the postcard Albarracin, entirely on foot, with the town's best restaurants, guesthouses, and viewpoints. Charming but cramped, with almost no parking or modern amenities inside the walls.
bestFor: short-stay remote workers wanting the full historic experience
pros: Walkable to everything in the old town

name: Portal de Molina
description: The historic entrance arch near the Guadalaviar river, where the old town meets the newer edge of the village. A natural first stop for arrivals by car, with easier parking than deeper in the old town and a pleasant riverside walk. Slightly less steep and more accessible than the upper lanes, good for those wary of constant climbing.
bestFor: those wanting old-town proximity without the steepest climbs
pros: Easier parking than the upper old town
Short walk into the historic core
cons: Still limited dining and shop options

name: Below the Walls
tagline: Quiet lower streets beneath the ramparts
description: The gentler, lower streets skirting the base of Albarracin's medieval walls, mixing a few modern guesthouses with traditional homes. More affordable and slightly roomier than inside the walls, with short walks up into the old town and easier access to whatever parking exists nearby. A practical, low-key base for a longer stay.
bestFor: longer stays wanting a bit more space and easier access
pros: More affordable than the old town core
Still a short walk to everything

name: Gea de Albarracin
description: A small farming village a short drive from Albarracin, offering cheaper rentals, a slower pace, and genuine rural Aragonese life without the tourist day-trip crowds. A car is essential from here, but it suits anyone wanting maximum quiet and lower costs while staying close enough to enjoy Albarracin regularly.
bestFor: budget-conscious nomads wanting rural isolation with Albarracin nearby
pros: Lower cost of living than Albarracin itself
cons: Car essential, no local bus reliability
Almost no amenities in the village itself
